reasons: Both answers correct the 'no harm' premise, reject the MySQL speed argument, add a pre-check, and still ship an ALTER that includes body instead of limiting the script to the safe columns. B covers both failure modes rubric item 1 names (the ALTER failing, and silent data loss if values are truncated via USING left()). It also gives a clearer go/no-go rule: stop if the body pre-check returns anything above zero. Its CHECK ... NOT VALID plus VALIDATE compromise avoids a long lock, while A's compromise is sound but slightly less operationally careful.
